2025 MESSAGE

Chairman’s message
Dear shareholders, partners, and customers!
2025 is a crucial year for BIDV's operations. It is not only a 
decisive year in implementing BIDV's overall development 
strategy for the 2021-2025 period, but also a milestone 
to truly assess the implementation capacity, the level of 
achievement of strategic goals, and the quality of growth of 
the entire system. With the decisive, proactive, and innovative 
leadership of the Board of Directors; the spirit of unity, 
discipline, and responsibility of the entire system; and the 
trust, cooperation, and partnership of shareholders, partners, 
and customers, BIDV has successfully achieved its set goals; 
creating a foundation, room for growth, and new momentum 
for the next development phase, ensuring that BIDV enters a 
new strategic cycle with a proactive mindset, strong internal 
capabilities, and a long-term vision.
Building the foundation for sustainable development
In 2025, despite the continued complex developments in 
the world, with more challenges than opportunities, our 
country still achieved great accomplishments and historical 
milestones: "reorganizing the country, streamlining the 
political system, removing bottlenecks and obstacles"; 
completing 15 out of 15 socio-economic development targets, 
maintaining macroeconomic stability, GDP growth of 8.02%; 
inflation at 3.31%, ensuring major balances; stable interest 
rates and exchange rates; and a safe and efficient operation 
of the credit institution system...
to 2024 and nearly double that of the beginning of 2021, 
continuing to lead the market in terms of credit market share 
– clearly reflecting BIDV's role as a key capital channel in the 
economy, and demonstrating its ability to achieve safe and 
reasonable growth amidst numerous fluctuations. The credit 
structure is shifting towards efficiency and sustainability, with 
strong growth in medium- and long-term loans, retail loans, 
and FDI loans.
A very important point is that BIDV's growth in scale is always 
accompanied by efficiency and quality: (i) Consolidated 
pre-tax profit reached VND37,788 billion, an 17.8% increase 
compared to 2024 and a threefold increase compared to 
2021; (ii) Profitability indicators improved positively compared 
to the previous year: ROA reached 1.01%; ROE reached 
19.43%; (iii) Credit quality was controlled within limits, the non-
performing loan ratio according to Circular 31/2024/TT-NHNN 
was controlled at 1.26%...
BIDV also completed transactions to increase its charter 
capital, strengthening its financial capacity: charter capital 
reached VND70,214 billion; the bank's own equity reached 
VND163,017 billion, more than double compared to the 
beginning of the period, thereby preserving and effectively 
developing state capital in the bank; BIDV's market 
capitalization is among the market leaders, reaching over 
VND273,000 billion (equivalent to USD11 billion).
In addition, BIDV has fully fulfilled its obligations to the State: 
contributing VND12,821 billion to the state budget in 2025, 
with a cumulative total of over VND39,300 billion for the 
period 2021-2025, consistently ranking among the leading 
banks in Vietnam in terms of corporate income tax payments.
In particular, to support businesses and people in overcoming 
difficulties, BIDV proactively reduced costs. to lower lending 
interest rates. Over the past year, the bank has supported 
nearly 400,000 customers with interest rate reductions 
ranging from 0.5% to 2% per year, while also restructuring 
repayment terms for customers...
In terms of management and operations, 2025 also marks a 
significant turning point for BIDV as its motto "Responsibility 
- Streamlining - Efficiency - Accelerating Transformation" 
has not only been instilled in its understanding but has also 
been realized through concrete results, thereby resolving 
many fundamental issues and creating a favorable momentum 
for BIDV to continue its strong breakthroughs.
First and foremost, with a sense of responsibility, BIDV has 
seriously, actively, and effectively implemented the policies, 
directions, and operational guidelines of the Government 
and the State Bank of Vietnam. BIDV has issued timely and 
appropriate resolutions and action programs; at the same time, 
it has focused on managing its business plan synchronously 
and decisively, closely adhering to assigned targets... BIDV has 
also effectively implemented solutions to support people and 
businesses in accordance with general policies, ensuring its 
core, leading, and responsible role in the economy in the new 
situation. BIDV has implemented credit programs focusing on 
priority sectors and development drivers as directed by the 
Government and the State Bank of Vietnam. BIDV has also 
fully demonstrated its responsibility to shareholders, partners, 
customers, and employees throughout the system...
Regarding streamlining, BIDV has taken strong and 
synchronized steps in organizational restructuring, network 
reorganization, and business process reform. The governance 
model at the Head Office has been reviewed and adjusted 
to clarify functions and responsibilities, reduce overlap, and 
minimize "touch points" with branches. Network reorganization 
has been implemented decisively but cautiously, in line with 
the development strategy and practical conditions of each 
locality. In particular, streamlining processes and reducing 
administrative procedures, coupled with the application of 
technology, has significantly shortened processing time, 
improved customer service quality, and increased employee 
productivity. These movements have helped BIDV form a more 
streamlined, professional, and flexible organizational model.
Based on that foundation, BIDV's operational efficiency 
has significantly improved, reflected in growth in scale 
coupled with quality, efficiency, and safety. BIDV continues 
to preserve and steadily develop state capital, enhance 
financial capacity through capital increase transactions, 
and standardize and upgrade risk management practices in 
accordance with international best practices. BIDV's brand 
value and social reputation continue to be strengthened and 
widely disseminated through communication activities, social 
responsibility, and corporate culture.
In particular, accelerating transformation has become a 
driving force throughout development. BIDV is promoting 
the transformation of its core business model according 
to new trends, ensuring "efficiency, effectiveness, and 
efficiency." In the retail banking sector, BIDV is implementing 
a comprehensive retail banking transformation project across 
three aspects: Business, Organizational Model, and Technology. 
In this context, BIDV continues to affirm its position as a 
leading state-owned commercial bank, a crucial pillar of the 
national financial and banking system. The entire system 
has successfully achieved its goals and tasks: effectively 
implementing the Business Development Strategy to 2025, 
with a vision to 2030, along with 7 component strategies 
and the Restructuring Plan for the period 2021-2025; 
achieving management and operational capabilities close to 
international best practices; developing a strong high-quality 
workforce; standardizing and widely disseminating corporate 
culture; and continuously improving the lives of its employees. 
In particular, BIDV has comprehensively, synchronously, and 
outstandingly fulfilled all business plan targets assigned by 
the State Bank of Vietnam and the General Shareholders' 
Meeting; consistently maintaining high growth rates in scale, 
market share, and efficiency, creating a solid foundation for 
sustainable development.
By the end of 2025, BIDV's total assets reached over VND3.27 
trillion, a 20.5% increase compared to 2024 and 2.2 times 
higher than at the beginning of 2021, further solidifying its 
position as the largest commercial bank in Vietnam. Deposits 
reached VND2.43 trillion, a 13.7% increase, nearly double that 
of the beginning of 2021, accounting for 14.3% of the total 
deposit market share – demonstrating BIDV's prestige and the 
trust of organizations and individuals in the bank. Outstanding 
loans reached VND2.32 trillion, a 15.2% increase compared

Chairman’s message
In the wholesale banking sector, BIDV is undergoing a strong 
restructuring towards specialization, forming specialized 
customer and capital business segments, shifting from 
simply providing credit to offering comprehensive financial 
solutions for businesses and partners. Human resources 
management is also undergoing a strong transformation, 
moving towards a modern model through the implementation 
of policies for evaluating, classifying, and assigning staff 
based on competence; increasing the number of customer 
relationship managers; and shifting the sales staff structure 
to increase business efficiency. In technology operations, 
BIDV is transforming towards increased centralization and 
automation; strongly applying digital technology, big data, 
and modern solutions. 
With positive results across all aspects of its operations, in 
2025, BIDV continued to receive high praise and recognition 
from domestic and international organizations through 
prestigious awards: “Top 1,000 Largest Listed Companies 
in the World”, “Best Retail Bank in Vietnam” for the 10th 
consecutive year, “Best Private Banking Service in Vietnam” 
for the 3rd consecutive year, “Best Contact Center in Asia-
Pacific”, “Top 50 Best Listed Companies in Vietnam”, “Best 
Digital Transformation Bank in Vietnam”, “Outstanding Digital 
Transformation 
Enterprise”, 
“Sustainable 
Development 
Enterprise”, “Best Custodian and Supervisory Bank in Vietnam”, 
“Best Trade Finance and Supply Chain Bank in Vietnam”; “Best 
Workplace in Vietnam” for the third consecutive year,... and 
other important awards in many other areas of operation...
It can be affirmed that BIDV's performance in 2025 is the 
result of a persistent effort, closely linking business objectives 
with improving operational efficiency according to market 
principles. This demonstrates strong growth in scale, 
reflecting BIDV's in-depth and sustainable development... and 
clearly shows BIDV's overarching mission: serving the nation, 
making positive contributions to national development; 
bringing sustainable value to the State and shareholders; 
accompanying businesses and people in their development; 
making positive contributions to the social community; and 
increasingly caring for the material and spiritual well-being and 
working environment of its employees... This is also the solid 
foundation for BIDV to confidently move into a new phase of 
development with higher goals and greater aspirations.
Continuing our efforts to help bidv break through, reach 
new heights, and take off
Our country has officially entered a new era – an era of 
development, prosperity, and strength. This context places very 
high demands on financial institutions, especially commercial 
banks, which play a leading and dominant role in the economy. 
In this situation, BIDV clearly defines its responsibility as both 
conducting business safely and efficiently, and as a partner, 
leader, and driving force for macroeconomic development. 
BIDV must continue to affirm its role as the bank for large 
projects and key national programs, as an important financial 
instrument in implementing socio-economic development 
goals, contributing to the realization of the two centenary 
goals of the country: (i) By 2030, Vietnam will become a 
developing country with modern industry and high middle 
income; (ii) By 2045, it will become a developed socialist 
country with high income.
BIDV has proactively developed and submitted to the 
State Bank of Vietnam for consideration and approval its 
Development Strategy until 2030, with a vision to 2045, which 
sets the goal: “To build BIDV into a leading large, strong, 
and green banking and financial group in Southeast Asia, 
striving to be among the top 100 strongest banks in Asia 
by 2030 and among the top 50 by 2045.” 
For 2026, BIDV has set the motto “Discipline - Quality 
- Efficiency - Comprehensive Transformation” and is 
determined to make every effort to successfully implement 
the following strategic and key tasks: (i) Continuing to 
maintain sustainable development in the context of very 
large credit capital needs to ensure the high growth target of 
the economy; BIDV must both develop in scale and undergo 
strong transformation in depth, quality, and efficiency... (ii) 
Implementing breakthrough solutions to strengthen financial 
capacity, improve operational efficiency, and adapt to 
market fluctuations... (iii) Continuing to promote innovation, 
application of big data and artificial intelligence technologies, 
and digital transformation; innovation must become a new 
driving force for development; Digital technology, data, 
and artificial intelligence must become the core foundation 
for development... (iv) Continue to develop the customer 
base in both aspects: scale and quality, attracting new 
customers while retaining and more effectively exploiting 
the existing customer base... (v) Continue to refine and 
vigorously implement the Sustainable Development Strategy 
to maintain BIDV's pioneering role and leading position 
in green finance, green credit, and ESG governance... (vi) 
Promote the development of high-quality human resources, 
so that people are truly the center, the pillar, and the driving 
force of BIDV's development... (vii) Maximize the core values, 
traditional values, resources, fundamental driving forces, and 
the position that BIDV already has; while seeking new growth 
drivers for the entire BIDV Group ecosystem… 
The new era of the nation is opening up great opportunities, 
but also presenting BIDV with unprecedented demands and 
challenges. Therefore, the entire BIDV system will continue to 
nurture the aspiration for contribution, maximize collective 
intelligence, maintain discipline, transform challenges into 
opportunities, and translate strategic vision into concrete 
actions to quickly build BIDV into a “Large - Strong - Green 
- Friendly - Modern – Devoted Bank”. From there, BIDV will 
not only consolidate its pivotal role in the national financial and 
banking system, but also make a strong breakthrough, elevate 
its position, soar to new heights, and make increasingly 
worthy contributions to the cause of building a strong and 
prosperous nation.
On behalf of the BIDV Board of Directors, I would like to 
express my deepest gratitude to the Leadership Team and 
over 29,000 employees throughout the system – those who 
have dedicated themselves wholeheartedly, contributing 
their intellect and capabilities to create the outstanding 
achievements of BIDV today and will continue to write new 
chapters of success for the system in the future.
I would also like to express my sincere gratitude to our 
shareholders, partners, and customers who have always 
trusted, chosen, and accompanied BIDV throughout its 
development journey. Your trust and strong cooperation 
are the crucial foundation for BIDV's continuous growth, 
enhancing its corporate value and affirming its role as a 
leading commercial bank in the economy. On this new journey, 
BIDV is committed to further strengthening that trust through 
practical, transparent, and effective actions; together with 
you, creating sustainable values, and moving towards a safe, 
prosperous, and long-term future.
Best regards!
ON BEHALF OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS
Chairman
Phan Duc Tu

From the outset of formulating the long-term business plan for the period 2021–2025, BIDV identified “towards sustainable 
development” as a consistent objective across all banking activities, positioning green banking and green credit as key 
priorities. Accordingly, in the business strategy for the period 2021–2025 with a vision to 2030, BIDV focused on implementing 
green credit packages, allocating a certain proportion of financing to customers in renewable energy, clean energy, low 
carbon production and consumption sectors, and climate change adaptation, thereby contributing to the transition of the 
economy towards green growth, environmental protection, climate resilience, improved efficiency in the use of resources 
and energy, and demonstrating responsibility towards the community and the environment.
In the coming period, BIDV continues to identify “Green” as one of the three development pillars of “Large – Strong – 
Green”. BIDV is a pioneering bank in the market in developing and implementing the Sustainable Development and ESG 
Practice Strategy for the period 2026–2030 (ESG Strategy). Under the ESG Strategy, BIDV has set the overall objective of 
“Building BIDV into the leading bank in the Vietnamese market in green and sustainable development and ESG practices, 
ranking first in green credit outstanding balance, and contributing positively to the economic and social development and 
environmental protection of the country”, while establishing a system of specific objectives around the three pillars of 
Environmental – Social – Governance together with a comprehensive set of solutions and a clear, detailed implementation 
roadmap to integrate ESG objectives into the bank’s business activities. 
With a systematic and comprehensive approach in alignment with the context of the Vietnamese market and towards 
international practices, the ESG Strategy will serve as a compass guiding the entire BIDV system in realizing its ESG objectives.

risk management capabilities and ensuring systemic stability 
in accordance with the orientations of the State Bank of 
Vietnam (SBV).
The system of credit documents and regulations, along with 
CRM policies and strategies, is comprehensively developed 
for a minimum three-year period and is regularly reviewed 
and updated. These ensure compliance with SBV regulations, 
alignment with international best practices and BIDV’s risk 
appetite, while gradually integrating sustainable development 
factors into credit portfolio management.
BIDV’s risk management model is organized and operated 
based on the principles of independence and centralization, 
in line with the Basel Committee’s recommendations and in 
compliance with Circular 13/2018/TT-NHNN dated 18 May 
2018. The credit risk management process at BIDV is built in 
a synchronized and closed-loop manner, from loan appraisal 
to post-loan monitoring, with a clear segregation of duties 
among relevant departments to ensure the identification, 
measurement, monitoring, and control of credit risk.
BIDV continuously updates and improves its credit risk 
management process to be lean and efficient while ensuring 
strictness and safety in credit operations. 
In 2025, BIDV manages credit growth proactively and flexibly, 
aligned with the SBV’s orientation, simultaneously ensuring 
the dual objectives of supporting economic growth and 
controlling credit risk.

Economic risk
The SBV implemented synchronized solutions to facilitate 
access to bank credit for businesses and individuals, aiming 
to recover production and business, promote growth 
coupled with macroeconomic stability, control inflation, and 
advance digital and green transformations. By the end of 
2025, credit growth is estimated at 18.5% compared to the 
end of the previous year, the highest in many years. Credit 
flows were primarily concentrated in manufacturing, exports, 
infrastructure, SMEs, and high-tech agriculture, while credit to 
risky sectors was strictly controlled. Interest rates remained 
stable, and abundant systemic liquidity improved capital 
accessibility for businesses and households, reaching a 5-year 
high. Interbank interest rates tended to gradually increase 
during the year, particularly in December due to surging year-
end credit demand and localized liquidity tightening at some 
banks. Deposit rates rose rapidly from late November among 
non-state commercial banks, hovering around 5.5-5.7% for 
12-month tenors - a slight increase compared to late 2024, 
reflecting seasonal factors. Lending rates edged up in the final 
months but remained flat compared to the beginning of the 
year, driven by high credit growth to meet the Government’s 
growth target of over 8%. Meanwhile, deposit mobilization, 
despite positive growth, showed signs of slowing down in the 
final months. The USD/VND exchange rate in 2025 was less 
volatile than in 2024, depreciating 3.2% YTD despite the USD 
strength (DXY Index) declining 9.1% from the beginning of the 
year. Global and domestic gold prices surged by 65% and 82% 
in 2025, respectively. The legal framework for monetary and 
banking activities was prioritized for improvement, ensuring 
safe operations, alignment with practical requirements, and 
adherence to international standards and practices.
Amidst international and domestic challenges, BIDV has 
proactively conducted timely analysis and assessment to 
develop flexible response scenarios for market fluctuations.

External risks, (i) Geopolitical risks and trade-technology

of natural disasters, climate change, and non-traditional risks

As Vietnam accelerates its transformation toward becoming 
a major regional financial hub capable of competing with 
international centers like Singapore and Hong Kong, the 
development and refinement of the legal system - particularly 
laws governing Credit Institutions (CIs) - is a critical imperative. 
A new, stringent, and internationally-aligned legal framework 
is considered the vital foundation for the safe and sustainable 
development of joint-stock commercial banks, including BIDV.
Vietnam’s legal system and economic policies have recently 
been developed in a relatively synchronized manner, 
fundamentally aligning with market economy mechanisms 
and international integration requirements. In the context 
of implementing the reorganization of administrative units 
and the transition to a two-tier local government model, the 
National Assembly has passed several key laws and resolutions 
to refine the legal environment for business operations and 
the banking and finance sector.
Key Laws and Resolutions Issued in 2024–2025
The National Assembly has issued numerous legal documents 
with direct and profound impacts on enterprises and CIs, 
including: Resolution 202/2025/QH15 on the arrangement of 
province-level administrative units; the Law on Notarization 
2024; the Law amending and supplementing the Law on 
the Organization of the People’s Procuracy 2025; the Law 
amending and supplementing the Law on Enterprises 2025; 
the Law on Personal Data Protection 2025; Resolution No. 
05/2025/NQ-CP on the pilot crypto-asset market; and 
Resolution 222/2025/QH15 on International Financial Centers 
in Vietnam.
These new regulations have created fundamental changes in 
the legal environment, specifically:
 
•
	
The Law on Notarization 2024: Clarifies the scope of 
notarization, the authority of notaries, and prohibited acts; 
defines liability for damages; expands cases for out-of-office 
notarization; and adds provisions for e-notarization.
 
•
	
The Amended Law on the Organization of the People’s 
Procuracy: Expands the power to supervise judicial activities 
and reorganizes the Procuracy system under a new model.
Legal risk
 
•
	
The Amended Law on Enterprises: Adds provisions on 
beneficial owners, market pricing of contributed capital/
shares, prohibited acts, conditions for private bond 
placement, and strengthens state management over business 
registration.
 
•
	
The Law on Personal Data Protection: Prescribes sanctions; 
clarifies specific issues in the banking and finance sector; 
protects biometric data; and provides transitional guidance 
from Decree 13/2023/ND-CP.
 
•
	
The Resolution on the pilot crypto-asset market: Allows for the 
pilot issuance, trading, and provision of crypto-asset services 
for four participant groups; requires foreign investors to open 
VND payment accounts at authorized banks in Vietnam.
 
•
	
The Resolution on International Financial Centers: Prescribes 
the establishment of financial centers in Ho Chi Minh City and 
Da Nang; encourages modern financial activities, Fintech, 
and green finance; and regulates banking operation models, 
foreign exchange policies, investment, and land.
Key Guiding Decrees and Circulars in the Banking and 
Finance Sector
In 2025, the Government and the SBV continued to issue 
various guiding decrees, notably:
 
•
	
Decree 23/2025/ND-CP on electronic signatures and trust 
services, introducing the concept of “trust services” and 
detailing the content and validity period of digital signature 
certificates.
 
•
	
Decree 70/2025/ND-CP amending regulations on invoices and 
documents, expanding the scope to foreign suppliers, and 
prescribing the timing of invoice issuance and incentives for 
e-invoices.
 
•
	
Decree 
226/2025/ND-CP 
amending 
details 
for 
the 
implementation of the Land Law, abolishing the land price 
framework starting 15 August 2025, amending land valuation 
methods, and regulating land recovery adjustments due to 
planning changes.
 
•
	
A Group of 08 Decrees guiding the operations of International 
Financial Centers, providing comprehensive regulations on 
finance, banking, labor, land, foreign exchange, arbitration, 
and commodity trading.
The Amended Law on Credit Institutions 2025 and its 
Impact on Bad Debt Resolution at BIDV
Law No. 96/2025/QH15 amending and supplementing certain 
articles of the Law on Credit Institutions, effective from 15 
October 2025, is assessed to have a positive impact on BIDV’s 
NPL (Non-Performing Loan) recovery.
 
•
	
First, the right to seize collateral has been codified, providing 
a legal basis for BIDV to dispose of collateral without going 
through litigation or enforcement proceedings, thereby 
reducing recovery time and costs. This also improves 
borrowers’ repayment awareness; however, seizure must 
strictly comply with transparency requirements under Article 
198a and Decree 304/2025/ND-CP.
 
•
	
Second, provisions on the distraint of collateral under Article 
198b ensure BIDV’s priority in collateral disposal, restricting 
enforcement agencies from distraining assets without the 
Bank’s consent, in line with the principle of “enforceability 
against third parties” under the Civil Code 2015.
 
•
	
Third, provisions on the return of collateral used as evidence 
in Article 198c inherit the spirit of Resolution 42, protecting 
BIDV’s right to dispose of collateral involved in criminal cases. 
However, the additional condition requiring security contracts 
to include an explicit agreement on the right of seizure is 
considered not entirely appropriate and requires further 
refinement.
Trends in Debt Resolution through Rehabilitation, 
Bankruptcy, and Court Litigation
The Law on Rehabilitation and Bankruptcy 2025 (effective 1 
March 2026), which introduces corporate rehabilitation as 
an independent procedure, is expected to be widely applied, 
enabling businesses to recover and continue debt repayment 
to CIs.
In judicial activities, while Courts generally protect the 
legitimate rights of CIs, practical obstacles remain, particularly 
in identifying CIs as “bona fide third parties.” Official Letter 
No. 02/TANDTC-PC from the Supreme People’s Court requires 
CIs to conduct rigorous appraisal and verification of collateral 
- an issue that BIDV and other banks continue to advocate for 
a more suitable application guidance.
Although Vietnam’s banking legal system has undergone 
significant refinement, it remains in a continuous adjustment 
process to align with international standards. Future legal 
changes are unpredictable and beyond BIDV’s control; 
therefore, legal risk is still considered a potential risk for 
investors and banking operations in the current context of 
deep integration.

Business situation
Total assets of the banking business alone reached VND3,265,519 billion, up 
20.5% compared to 2024. BIDV maintained its position as the largest commercial 
bank by total assets in Vietnam.  
Mobilized capital (1) was aligned with credit growth, adequately meeting capital 
use needs while ensuring safety and efficiency: total mobilized funds as at 31 
December 2025 reached VND3,052,107 billion; of which deposits from organizations 
and residents reached VND2,427,835 billion, up 13.7% compared to the beginning of 
the year.
Total outstanding credit and investment (2) reached VND3,098,740 billion; of 
which outstanding credit reached VND2,324,935 billion, up 15.2% compared to 2024, 
in compliance with the credit limit assigned by the State Bank of Vietnam. BIDV 
maintained the leading position by loans to economic organizations and residents 
among joint stock commercial banks.
BIDV’s credit quality continued to be well controlled within the limits: the non-
performing loan ratio under Circular No. 31/2024/TT-NHNN as at 31 December 
2025 was maintained at 1.26%, meeting the target set by the State Bank of Vietnam 
(≤1.6%). The bad debt coverage ratio of the commercial banking business as at 31 
December 2025 reached 101%. 
Net service income (excluding guarantee fees) reached VND5,708 billion, up 
1.4% compared to 2024 (if excluding the impact of adjusting the accounting of 
several trade finance products to other income from credit activities from 1 July 
2024 according to the Law on Credit Institutions 2024, net service income grew 
by 10.7%); Service lines with good growth compared to 2024 included payment 
service income (up 11%), of which trade finance service income increased by 19% 
(compared to same data of 2024).
Net income from forex trading in 2025 reached VND3,718 billion, down 29.4% 
compared to 2024 due to unfavorable market conditions, strong exchange rate 
fluctuations and at levels close to the regulatory limits of the State Bank of Vietnam.
Total operating income of the commercial banking business in 2025 reached 
VND184,247 billion, exceeding the plan assigned by the State Bank of Vietnam.
Business management expenses were controlled in line with business conditions: 
in 2025, expenses increased by 9.5% compared to 2024; the cost to income ratio 
(CIR) was 32.7%, lower than in 2024 (33.5%) and at a low level compared to practices 
(≤45%).
Net operating income of the commercial banking business in 2025 reached 
VND58,081 billion, an increase of 13.4% compared to 2024.
Profit before tax of the commercial banking business in 2025 reached VND35,509 
billion, up 15.7% compared to 2024, exceeding the plan assigned by the State Bank of 
Vietnam and the General Meeting of Shareholders (VND32,000 billion).
Consolidated profit before tax reached VND37,788 billion, increasing by 17.8% 
compared to 2024. Provisioning for credit risks was fully made in accordance with 
regulations.
Operational safety ratios were ensured in compliance with the regulations of 
the State Bank of Vietnam.

In 2025, BIDV focused on strengthening to attract and develop a team of experts in the 
field of digital banking, aiming to accelerate the development of a modern banking 
system through advanced digital banking services and digital internal governance, in 
line with both industry trends and Vietnam’s broader digital transformation agenda.
In 2025, the number of employees of BIDV’s commercial banking business reached 
26,280 (up 185 compared to 2024). The total number of employees (including 
managers) of the bank and its subsidiaries was 29,273.
In terms of gender structure, men accounted for 41.32% and women 58.68% - a 
distribution consistent with most institutions in the banking and finance sector. 
In terms of workforce quality, over 96.5% of employees held at least a bachelor’s 
degree, and the average age was approximately 37.7 years.

Over 19 years of development and growth, VRB has consistently 
strived to overcome challenges arising from complex global 
developments and the domestic economic context, gradually 
expanding its scale, strengthening its market position, and 
building a solid foundation toward becoming an efficient bank.
The year 2025 marked an important milestone for VRB, 
reflecting significant achievements with a strong profit 
breakthrough, sustainable growth in scale, and well-controlled 
credit quality. Mobilized capital increased by 3%, loans to 
customers grew by 14%, and the non-performing loan ratio 
was maintained at 1.01%. Notably, profit before tax reached 
VND1,016 billion, up 65% compared to 2024, and ROE 
reached 18.5%, the highest level since its establishment. VRB 
also continued to ensure compliance with prudential ratios 
as prescribed by the State Bank of Vietnam, while further 
strengthening its risk management framework in line with 
Basel II standards and practices.
With the aim of contributing to the development of the 
national aviation industry, and under the approval of the Prime 
Minister, Vietnam Aircraft Leasing Joint Stock Company (VALC) 
officially commenced operations at the end of 2007. Since 
its establishment, VALC has gradually affirmed its position in 
both the domestic and international aircraft leasing markets 
through the successful implementation of two major aircraft 
purchase and lease projects (5 ATR 72-500 aircrafts and 10 
Airbus A321-200 aircrafts). In addition, VALC has studied and 
developed several joint investment projects, including engine 
leasing and other aviation equipment leasing.
In 2025, VALC completed its asset restructuring plan and 
recorded breakthrough business results. Total revenue 
reached USD363.8 million, profit before tax reached USD114 
million, and ROE was ~44.5%.

REPORT ON GREEN CAPITAL MARKET ACTIVITIES
Sustainable Deposit Framework – setting 
standards for responsible capital mobilization
In 2025, BIDV issued a Sustainable Deposit Framework, 
developed in full compliance with the current regulations 
of the State Bank of Vietnam on term deposits, while 
referencing international practices and standards on 
sustainable finance. Accordingly, funds mobilized from 
deposit products labeled as “green”, “social” or “sustainable” 
are allocated to finance or refinance eligible projects 
under the Sustainable Loan Framework, which has been 
independently evaluated by Moody’s, thereby ensuring 
consistency across the bank’s ESG product portfolio. 
The application of the Sustainable Deposit Framework 
enables BIDV to proactively manage mobilization volumes 
in line with actual disbursement results, while establishing 
periodic review mechanisms to exclude projects that no 
longer meet eligibility criteria.
In terms of implementation principles, BIDV’s Sustainable 
Deposit Framework is built upon four core pillars, including 
(i) using proceeds strictly for eligible green and social 
projects; (ii) applying a rigorous project evaluation, selection 
and approval process that integrates environmental and 
social risk management throughout the credit lifecycle; 
(iii) maintaining transparent fund management, monitoring 
and accounting mechanisms; and (iv) providing periodic 
reporting on allocation and impact in line with international 
practices and BIDV’s disclosure requirements. These 
Pioneering the trend of sustainable development, in 2025 BIDV actively and 
proactively built and continued to lay solid foundations for green transition in line with 
international standards. BIDV provided comprehensive sustainable finance solutions, 
supporting enterprises in raising awareness, implementing and practicing ESG, as well 
as integrating sustainable governance into business operations, thereby creating new 
growth drivers in a constantly evolving market environment.

BIDV leads the market in financing green projects. As at 30 
September 2025, BIDV’s outstanding green credit reached 
VND81,234 billion. BIDV has consistently taken the lead in 
developing banking products and services to meet the 
credit demand of enterprises and investors participating in 
green and circular economy projects. BIDV not only provides 
effective financial solutions to support project owners but 
also continuously increases the proportion of bank credit 
allocated to projects in renewable energy, transportation, 
building materials production, agriculture, waste treatment 
and other low carbon emission sectors.
BIDV continues to affirm its pioneering role in implementing 
the policies of the Government and the State Bank of 
Vietnam on green growth and green credit, joining hands with 
enterprises to build a green economy and with the community 
toward sustainable development. In 2025, BIDV successfully 
rolled out a number of green credit packages, including the 
green textile package (with a scale of VND3,000 billion and 
USD50 million), the green building project financing package 
(with a scale of VND10,000 billion), the green credit program 
for financing clean water production and supply projects 
(with a scale of VND5,000 billion), and the green finance 
solution package supporting port enterprises (with a scale 
of VND2,000 billion). Participating enterprises benefit from 
preferential financing policies such as attractive lending rates, 
flexible financing structures, fast and timely disbursement, 
and advisory support from highly qualified experts and 
project finance specialists.
Green credit is identified by BIDV as one of the top priorities 
in its long-term business strategy. Building on its current 
green credit portfolio, BIDV expects to further increase the 
outstanding loans and the proportion of green credit annually, 
striving to maintain its position as one of the leading banks by 
green credit market share and scale in the market.
In 2023 and 2024, within the framework of the World Bank’s 
technical assistance and advisory program, BIDV published 
its Green Bond Framework and Sustainable Bond Framework. 
These frameworks were assessed by Moody’s as aligned with 
the Green Bond Principles and Sustainability Bond Guidelines 
of the International Capital Market Association (ICMA), 
receiving an SQS2 – Very Good rating. This affirms a high level 
of compliance and transparency in project selection, appraisal, 
lending processes, governance and reporting practices when 
issuing green and sustainable bonds in accordance with 
international principles and standards, while demonstrating 
BIDV’s capacity and reputation in the green finance market.
BIDV has successfully and consistently issued green bonds and 
sustainable bonds on an annual basis, with cumulative issuance 
reaching VND8,350 billion by 2025, establishing its pioneering 
and leading position in issuing green and sustainable bonds in 
line with international standards in the domestic market.
In each year of issuance, BIDV has fully disbursed the 
proceeds to eligible green and social projects immediately 
after successful issuance. To date, 100% of the green and 
sustainable bond proceeds have been allocated to eligible 
projects in renewable energy, sustainable transportation, 
green buildings, sustainable water management and social 
housing, in accordance with the published Green Bond and 
Sustainable Bond Frameworks.
Fulfilling its commitments to investors, BIDV has issued fund 
allocation and impact reports for projects financed by green 
and sustainable bond proceeds over two consecutive reporting 
periods. These reports have been independently reviewed 
by reputable domestic rating organizations, completed and 
disclosed to investors, ensuring transparency to the market.

“Best Issuer for Sustainable Finance in Vietnam 2025” by The

AFFIRMING PIONEERING STRENGTH AND THE ROLE OF A KEY BANK OF THE 
ECONOMY, EXCELLENTLY COMPLETING THE 2025 BUSINESS PLAN
Over nearly 70 years of construction and development, BIDV is proud 
to be the longest-established commercial bank, always striving to 
serve the Fatherland and contribute positively to the glorious cause 
of national construction and development. In 2025, BIDV continued 
to affirm its position as the bank with the largest operating scale in 
Vietnam for many consecutive years, with total assets exceeding 
VND3.27 quadrillion, ranking first in the market and becoming the 
first bank to surpass the VND3 quadrillion mark; total outstanding 
credit and investment reached VND3.09 quadrillion, focusing on 
production and business sectors, priority sectors, and growth 
drivers in line with the Government’s policies and the SBV’s direction, 
of which outstanding credit exceeded VND2.32 quadrillion, up 15.2% 
compared to the beginning of the year, maintaining the leading 
market position in credit market share; total mobilized funds reached 
VND3.05 quadrillion; of which funds mobilized from organizations 
and residents reached VND2.43 quadrillion, managed in alignment 
with credit growth developments, ensuring safety and efficiency. 
At the same time, in 2025, BIDV excellently completed the business 
plan targets: total income reached VND184,200 billion, fulfilling 
110% of the plan; total expenses amounted to VND148,738 billion, 
the expense growth was controlled at a level lower than income and 
profit growth; profit before tax of the commercial banking business 
reached VND35,509 billion, fulfilling 111% of the plan; consolidated 
profit before tax reached VND37,788 billion; credit quality was 
controlled within limits, with the non-performing loan ratio under 
Circular No. 31/2024/TT-NHNN at 1.26%, in line with the SBV’s 
orientation targets.
In 2025, in addition to excellently completing the business plan, BIDV 
also continued to be one of the leading banks in implementing the 
policies and directives of the Government and the SBV, actively 
and effectively implementing solutions to support people and 
businesses, fulfilling its responsibility to the economy in the new 
context. BIDV proactively reduced income and operating expenses 
to lower lending interest rates to support customers, with reductions 
ranging from 0.5% to 2% per year depending on customer groups; 
restructured debt repayment schedules and maintained debt 
classification to support customers facing difficulties; actively 
implemented preferential credit programs such as social housing 
loans and disbursement to remove difficulties in the agriculture, 
forestry, and fisheries sectors; continued to play a pioneering role 
in coordinating with regulatory authorities to promote national 
digital transformation and cashless payments, etc. State capital at 
BIDV was also preserved and developed, with owners’ equity as of 
31 December 2025 reaching VND163,017 billion, up 19.6% compared 
to 2024; BIDV’s market capitalization reached VND273 trillion 
(equivalent to USD10.5 billion), among the largest on the Vietnamese 
stock market. BIDV also fully fulfilled its obligations to the State in 
accordance with regulations, contributing VND12,821 billion to the 
State budget, achieving 100% of the 2025 estimate.
CONSOLIDATING THE ORGANIZATIONAL MODEL, STREAMLINING THE NETWORK, 
SIMPLIFYING PROCESSES ASSOCIATED WITH ACCELERATING TRANSFORMATION, 
ENHANCING PERFORMANCE, EFFECTIVENESS, AND EFFICIENCY ACROSS THE 
ENTIRE SYSTEM
In 2025, BIDV streamlined its operating apparatus and consolidated 
the governance model at the Head Office through reviewing, 
adjusting, and comprehensively planning the functions, duties, and 
coordination mechanisms of each unit, minimizing touchpoints for 
branches; simplifying processes across multiple areas of operation 
to remove bottlenecks, improve operational efficiency, accelerate 
decision-making, and promote optimization at the Head Office.
At the same time, BIDV decisively implemented the restructuring 
of its operational network, completing the arrangement of 16 
branches (terminating operations of 08 branches, converting 4 
branches into Transaction Offices (TOs), and upgrading 4 branches 
under specialized models) and 94 Transaction Offices (terminating 
operations of 07 TOs, changing managing branches for 55 TOs, and 
orienting relocation for 32 TOs). The units after restructuring quickly 
stabilized operations, ensuring smooth continuity without disrupting 
customer service, creating a foundation to fully exploit market 
potential and enhance competitiveness in their operating areas.
BIDV also reviewed and streamlined its workforce, implementing 
policies for employees retiring early upon request and for employees 
affected by the restructuring and adjustment of labor structure, 
organizational structure, and network within BIDV, ensuring 
transparency, openness, and humanity.
Notably, in 2025, BIDV also accelerated the transformation of 
its core business operating model in line with new trends. The 
comprehensive retail banking transformation project continued to 
be implemented synchronously and methodically, helping to shape 
segment-based business, innovate sales management thinking and 
methods, and promote the application of technology and big data 
in business operations; operational transformation was carried out 
toward increased specialization and automation (completion of 
Phase 1 of the Centralized Treasury Operations Project, expansion of 
centralized asset valuation to 03 regional clusters, implementation 
of the project on centralizing remittance operations at BIDV through 
2030, etc.)
STRENGTHENING TECHNOLOGICAL MASTERY, PROMOTING DIGITAL 
TRANSFORMATION AND APPLICATION OF MODERN SCIENTIFIC ACHIEVEMENTS
The year 2025 marked a strong advancement for BIDV in its journey 
to modernize digital infrastructure and enhance technological 
self-reliance, viewing data and digital transformation as drivers of 
rapid and sustainable growth.
The digital financial ecosystem continued to expand, with the 
vast majority of BIDV’s products and services fully digitized, 
providing seamless, secure, and intelligent experiences for 
customers. BIDV’s information technology system clearly shifted 
from a supporting role to directly creating value by independently 
implementing most key projects, generating benefits worth 
trillions of VND. Many digital platforms developed by BIDV have 
become operational pillars, such as the B.One system, which 
establishes a comprehensive and rapid digital internal governance 
environment; the AI Chatbot virtual assistant function - AskBee 
- supporting convenient consultation and document retrieval; 
deployment of a completely new digital banking system for 
corporate customers - BIDV Direct - providing an advanced 
and modern financial service ecosystem to help enterprises 
improve operational efficiency and promote business growth; 
mastering the Core Banking Profile system, self-operating and 
comprehensively upgrading the system.
Management and operation of the IT system remained safe 
and smooth despite the high volume of transactions across all 
systems; strict processes were established, with regular updates 
of software, equipment, and technical security to prevent 
vulnerabilities and promptly address any incidents that may arise.
The global economy in 2025 continued to improve in growth but still contained many 
risks under the pressure of trade tensions, reciprocal tax policies, and escalating 
geopolitical conflicts. Amid global economic uncertainties, Vietnam emerged as a 
bright spot of the world; GDP recorded impressive growth (8.02%), macroeconomic 
stability was maintained, and inflation was controlled; the economic structure, business 
environment, and people’s livelihoods improved positively; major balances were 
ensured, and the monetary market remained stable; foreign affairs and international 
integration activities were recognized and highly appreciated by the international 
community; notably, the “Reorganization of the nation” revolution opened up new 
development spaces, enabling Vietnam to confidently and firmly advance into an era 
of strong rise toward wealth, prosperity, and flourishing development.
In that context, the entire BIDV system demonstrated solidarity, strong determination, 
and concerted efforts, comprehensively exceeding the targets and tasks assigned by 
the State Bank of Vietnam and the General Meeting of Shareholders across all aspects: 
scale, structure, quality, efficiency, and institutional development; ensuring full 
benefits for shareholders while improving income and employment for employees; 
continuing to effectively implement the national monetary policy, promoting its core, 
key, and leading role in guiding the market; contributing to economic growth and 
maintaining the safe and sound development of the system of credit institutions.
The outstanding results of the BIDV system in 2025 are reflected in the following 
operational aspects:

RESOURCE QUALITY AND LABOR PRODUCTIVITY
In 2025, BIDV consolidated its leadership team and key personnel 
of the bank: (i) elected an additional 01 member of the Board of 
Directors and 01 member of the Supervisory Board for the 2022–

qualifications and skills according to job positions, competency 
frameworks, and specialized training in advanced knowledge/
skills and priority areas; ... as a result, income and labor 
productivity improved and remained at a highly competitive level 
compared to the market.

Management results in 2025
In 2025, Vietnam’s economy recorded an impressive recovery, 
with GDP growth of 8.02% and inflation controlled at around 
3.5%. Total import and export turnover remained high at over 
USD920 billion, reflecting a strong rebound in trade activities. 
Despite continued complex and unpredictable developments 
in the global environment, Vietnam successfully overcame 
challenges, laying a solid foundation for pursuing double digit 
GDP growth in the coming period.
The State Bank of Vietnam regulated the monetary policy in a 
proactive and flexible manner, closely coordinating with fiscal 
policy to control inflation and stabilize the money and foreign 
exchange markets, while maintaining major macroeconomic 
balances. Credit growth was directed toward safety; lending 
rates were maintained reasonably to support the recovery 
of production and business activities; promoting digital 
transformation, innovation, and cashless payments. The 
legal framework on monetary and banking was improved in 
line with practical requirements and international standards 
and practices, thereby contributing to enhancing the system 
safety.
Specific business performance
1
In 2025, BIDV’s business operations were conducted safely, smoothly, and efficiently, 
successfully fulfilling all business plan targets assigned by the State Bank of Vietnam 
and the General Meeting of Shareholders. In 2025, BIDV was also recognized with 
prestigious rankings, including Top 5 most valuable brands in Vietnam, up 182 places 
to rank 899th in the list of the 2,000 largest public companies in the Forbes Global 
2000 ranking, reflecting the bank’s growing prestige and stature in the market.
Growth in assets, credit, and deposits: 
In 2025, BIDV achieved outstanding scale expansion, with 
total assets reaching VND3.27 quadrillion, up 20.5% compared 
to 2024, becoming the first bank to surpass the VND3 
quadrillion milestone and affirming its position as the largest 
joint stock commercial bank in Vietnam. Outstanding credit 
reached VND2,324,935 billion, up 15.2% compared to 2024, 
accounting for 12.5% of total credit in the economy, with a 
focus on production sectors and priority areas aligned with 
the Government’s policies, the direction of the State Bank 
of Vietnam, and BIDV’s business orientation. Total mobilized 
capital reached VND2,427,835 billion, up 13.7% compared to 
2024. The deposit structure improved, with the CASA ratio 
reaching 17.52%, contributing to maintaining effective capital 
mobilization and utilization. The loan to deposit ratio (LDR) 
was controlled at 81.81%, within the regulatory limit set by the 
State Bank of Vietnam (≤85%).
Income and profitability:
Despite ongoing challenges in the business environment, BIDV 
maintained positive growth in both income and profitability. 
Total operating income in 2025 reached VND184,247 billion, 
up 10.4% compared to 2024, achieving 110% of the planned 
target. Non-interest income (from services, foreign exchange 
trading, etc.) contributed positively, driven by the expansion 
of retail banking activities and product diversification. Net 
interest income reached VND61,225 billion, up 8.9% compared 
to 2024, supported by strong credit growth alongside an 
effective restructuring of the balance sheet toward higher-
yielding assets, and the promotion of low-cost funding 
sources (demand deposits recorded strong growth of 24.1%, 
with the average CASA ratio reaching 17.52%, higher than 
16.55% in the previous year), thereby improving funding costs 
and enhancing BIDV’s competitiveness. In parallel with income 
growth, BIDV effectively controlled operating expenses, with 
the cost to income ratio (CIR) decreasing to 32.7% in 2025 
(compared to 33.5% in 2024).
As a result, BIDV’s profit before tax reached VND35,509 
billion, up 15.7% compared to 2024. Consolidated profit 
after tax reached VND30,430 billion, up 18.5%. Return on 
equity exceeded 19%, ensuring benefits for shareholders and 
investors.
Asset quality control (non-performing loans):
Credit risk management was given special focus by BIDV in 
2025, with the quality of the credit portfolio maintained within 
safe limits. The non-performing loan ratio according to Circular 
31/2024/TT-NHNN was controlled at 1.26%, significantly 
lower than the 1.6% ceiling allowed by the State Bank of 
Vietnam. The group 2 loan ratio stood at 1.15%, maintained 
at a low level compared to the internal threshold (≤3%). The 
bank proactively conducted debt classification and made 
adequate risk provisions, with the bad debt coverage ratio 
of the commercial banking business reaching 101.1%, thereby 
enhancing its readiness to address potential credit risks.

Currently, BIDV has five committees under its Board of Directors, including: the Risk Management Committee, the Human 
Resources Committee, the Strategy and Organization Committee, the Information Technology Committee, and the BIDV-
Hana Bank Strategic Cooperation Committee. The Board of Directors has issued separate regulations on the organization and

In 2025, the Committees fully and promptly carried out their functions and duties as stipulated in the organizational and 
operational regulations of each Committee. The specific results achieved are as follows:
Risk Management Committee
The Risk Management Committee, reporting directly to the 
Board of Directors, performs the function of advising and 
consulting on issues related to risk management throughout 
the entire BIDV system to enhance the effectiveness of the 
risk management system and establish a risk control culture 
throughout the BIDV system. In 2025, the Risk Management 
Committee will continue to fully implement its functions and 
tasks as stipulated in Circular 13, including: (i) Advising on the 
development, management, and supervision of the Bank's 
overall Risk Management Framework; (ii) Advising the Board 
of Directors on monitoring the implementation of key risk 
limits and operational safety indicators; (iii) Advising the Board 
of Directors on supervising the General Director in addressing 
risk management limitations according to the requirements 
of the State Bank of Vietnam, independent auditors, internal 
auditors, and other relevant agencies.
The activities of the Risk Management Committee fully 
comply with the regulations of the State Bank of Vietnam 
and adopt good practices in banking risk management. The 
recommendations of the Risk Management Committee have 
contributed to timely warning, risk prevention, and ensuring 
the safety of the system's operations.

Organization for conducting internal audits:
The Supervisory Board has provided guidance, direction, 
and regular supervision to the Internal Audit Department in 
implementing the 2025 audit plan, promptly adjusting the audit 
plan to suit the actual operations and the direction of the BIDV 
Board of Directors. Accordingly, the Internal Audit Department 
has completed 100% of the audit plan, ensuring both progress 
and quality. Specifically, in 2025, the Internal Audit Department 
conducted direct audits at 32 branches covering several activities 
including credit, financial management, asset management, 
treasury management, and information technology; audits at 
10 Boards/Centers of the State Treasury on credit operations; 
operational risk management for outsourcing activities; market 
risk management and concentration risk in proprietary trading; 
internal assessment of capital adequacy; centralized asset 
procurement; treasury management; information technology; 
anti-money laundering, counter-terrorism financing, and anti-
proliferation of weapons of mass destruction; Audit of BIDV 
Securities Joint Stock Company regarding governance, internal 
control, and financial management. 
The audit results show that, in general, the units have complied 
with the legal mechanisms, policies, and internal procedures and 
regulations of BIDV. The errors and shortcomings discovered by 
the internal audit have been seriously rectified and addressed by 
the units. Recommendations on strengthening internal control 
and improving the quality of audit operations/activities have 
been acknowledged by BIDV's leadership and directed to be 
implemented by the units. The Supervisory Board has directed 
the development and approval of the 2026 internal audit plan 
and reported it to the State Bank of Vietnam on schedule.
Through the direction and supervision of internal audit activities in 
2025 and the results of the internal audit in 2025, the Supervisory 
Board assesses that the Head of Internal Audit and the internal 
auditors have successfully completed their tasks in 2025, fully 
meeting the standards, adhering to professional ethics and 
codes of conduct as prescribed by BIDV in the performance of 
their duties.

in 2025. The monitoring results show that equity capital is 
preserved and growing steadily, the capital adequacy ratio 
meets the regulations of the State Bank of Vietnam, and all

safety in operations comply with legal regulations.

2024 financial statements and 2025 semi-annual financial

truthfully, and reasonably reflect, in all material aspects, the 
consolidated and individual financial situation of BIDV; and 
are presented in accordance with the regulations of the State 
Bank of Vietnam, consistent with the accounting system 
of credit institutions, Vietnamese accounting standards,

IMPLEMENTATION OF CORPORATE GOVERNANCE REGULATIONS
Process of supervising and evaluating corporate governance
General assessment of corporate governance 
at BIDV
Process 
of 
monitoring 
and 
evaluating 
corporate 
governance
BIDV conducts monitoring, supervision and evaluation of 
corporate governance activities on the basis of compliance 
with applicable laws and regulations, the BIDV Charter 
and internal regulations, including the Regulation on the 
organization and operation of the Board of Directors and the 
internal governance regulation.
With the aim of orienting corporate governance towards 
regional and global Good practices, BIDV have researched 
and applied (i) OECD Principles of Corporate Governance, (ii) 
ASEAN Corporate Governance Scorecard and (iii) Principles of 
Corporate Governance according to best practices for public 
companies in Vietnam jointly developed by the State Securities 
Commission and the International Finance Corporation IFC. 
Accordingly, the Person in charge of corporate governance 
at BIDV submitted reports to the BOD for approval on the 
process and criteria for supervising and evaluating corporate 
governance at BIDV.
Periodically on 30 June and 31 December each year, the focal 
unit under the BOD (The Secretariat and Investor Relations) 
shall coordinate with relevant units in the system to evaluate 
corporate governance at BIDV according to the criteria of 
the ASEAN Corporate Governance Scorecard. The person in 
charge of corporate governance is responsible for directing 
and approving the content of the Report before submitting 
the Report to the Board of Directors for approval. 
The evaluation results are consolidated and reported in the 
annual report and serve as a basis for proposing solutions to 
improve and enhance the quality of corporate governance 
for consideration by the Board of Directors and the Board of 
Management.
BIDV is committed to implementing corporate governance in 
compliance with legal regulations on corporate governance 
applicable to large public companies, including the Law 
on Enterprises, the Law on Credit Institutions, the Law on 
Securities, Circular No. 116/2020/TT-BTC of the Ministry 
of Finance providing guidance on a number of articles on 
corporate governance applicable to public companies, 
Circular No. 96/2020/TT-BTC of the Ministry of Finance 
providing guidance on information disclosure on the 
securities market, and other relevant legal documents. At the 
same time, BIDV strictly complies with its internal corporate 
governance regulations, such as the Charter on organization 
and operation of BIDV, the internal governance regulation, the 
Regulation on the organization and operation of the Board 
of Directors, and the Regulation on the organization and 
operation of the Supervisory Board. Contents of the disclosed 
information, semi-annual and annual corporate governance 
reports, and the annual report are prepared in accordance 
with regulations, ensuring completeness, timeliness and 
transparency. BIDV has also appointed the person in charge 
of corporate governance in accordance with applicable 
regulations.
In recent years, in addition to complying with current 
regulations on corporate governance, BIDV has researched 
and applied the OECD Principles of Corporate Governance, 
the ASEAN Corporate Governance Scorecard, the Principles of 
Corporate Governance according to best practices for public 
companies in Vietnam jointly developed by the State Securities 
Commission and the International Finance Corporation IFC. 
In 2023, after the OECD Principles of Corporate Governance 
were revised with a new Chapter on “Sustainable and 
Resilient Development” related to ESG contents and the 
ASEAN Corporate Governance Scorecard Questionnaire was 
updated to add ESG assessment questions corresponding to 
the OECD Code of Practices in the role with related parties 
section, BIDV updated the corporate governance assessment 
contents related to these contents and conducted corporate 
governance scoring from 31 December 2023.
BIDV's specific corporate governance targets include: (i) 
ensuring the rights of shareholders, investors and related 
parties; (ii) enhancing publicity and transparency in the 
Bank's operations; (iii) effectively operating the corporate 
governance system; (iv) ensuring the operational efficiency of 
the Board of Directors, the Supervisory Board and the Board 
of Management; (v) linking corporate governance targets 
with sustainable development.
Process 
of 
supervising 
and 
monitoring 
the 
implementation of strategies
The role of the BOD in supervising, monitoring the strategies 
is clearly and specifically defined.
Currently, the development, implementation, evaluation, and 
supervising of the strategies at BIDV are implemented in 
accordance with the Regulations on Strategic governance. 
Accordingly, the BOD is responsible for setting the strategic 
directions, directing the development, approving, issuing 
and comprehensively supervising the implementation of 
strategies in each period.
Supervising and evaluation of the implementation results of 
the strategies are implemented on a monthly, quarterly and 
annual basis
The monthly and quarterly supervision is carried out through 
the strategy management. software program. With respect 
to annual supervision, BIDV conducts an annual assessment 
of the implementation of the Strategy and submits it to the 
Board of Directors in the first quarter each year, including 
but not limited to the following contents: a comprehensive 
assessment of the implementation results of priority 
objectives, business plan targets, BIDV’s competitive position, 
progress and results of the Strategy implementation plan, 
results of sub-component strategies, difficulties and obstacles 
encountered, and proposals for solutions to achieve the set 
strategic objectives if necessary.
During the process of supervising and evaluating the 
implementation of the Strategy, if economic, political, social 
conditions and other macro factors undergo significant 
changes that may materially impact or affect the need to 
change, adjust or update the overall Strategy, whether 
creating challenges or opening up new opportunities, BIDV 
will prepare a report assessing the impact of such macro 
changes and propose adjustments or supplements to the 
overall Strategy if necessary.

Protecting shareholder rights, promoting transparency 
and accountability
BIDV always prioritizes ensuring the full and equal protection 
of shareholders' legal rights, while emphasizing transparency, 
accuracy, 
and 
timeliness 
in 
information 
disclosure. 
Shareholders' rights are exercised in accordance with the 
law, BIDV's Charter, and relevant internal regulations. BIDV 
has issued a Handbook on the Exercise of Rights for Ordinary 
Shareholders, specifying the provisions of the law and BIDV's 
Charter into unified guidelines, contributing to ensuring that 
shareholders can fully exercise their rights in a transparent, 
consistent, and proper manner, following the prescribed 
procedures.
The Annual General Meeting of Shareholders (April 
2025) was held in accordance with regulations, enabling 
shareholders to promptly access information on the Bank's 
operations and business results, participate in discussions, 
contribute opinions, and vote on important issues within their 
authority. BIDV implemented remote voting/voting, allowing 
shareholders who could not attend the meeting to exercise 
their voting rights quickly, safely, and securely. Resolutions, 
minutes, and related documents of the meeting are fully 
published on BIDV's website.
Beyond the framework of the Annual General Meeting, 
BIDV encourages regular participation and interaction of 
shareholders and investors through investor conferences, 
regular meetings and outreach programs with shareholders 
and the investor community. Through these activities, 
shareholders can access information, exchange opinions, 
provide feedback, and engage in direct dialogue with the 
Bank, thereby contributing to increased transparency, 
accountability, and engagement between BIDV and its 
shareholders. The Investor Relations Department acts as the 
central point of contact in receiving, supporting, and promptly 
addressing requests and inquiries from shareholders and 
investors through various interaction channels such as 
telephone, email, and a chatbot on the website.
As a large-scale public company with listed stocks and bonds, 
BIDV fully, promptly, and transparently discloses information 
in accordance with the law. In 2025, BIDV disclosed 31 periodic 
items and 278 extraordinary items, related to financial 
statements, 
annual 
reports, 
sustainable 
development 
reports, corporate governance reports, activities of the 
General Meeting of Shareholders, transactions with related 
parties, insider information, and bond issuance... The Investor 
Relations Department also proactively coordinates with the 
media team to provide accurate information that reflects the 
true nature of the Bank's business operations; diversifying 
information channels to shareholders and implementing 
bilingual 
Vietnamese-English 
disclosure 
to 
meet 
the 
information access needs of shareholders and the domestic 
and international investment community.
Increase the frequency of contact with investors and 
improve the quality of information provided to the 
market.
BIDV's investor relations efforts continue to expand in scale 
and improve in quality, going beyond simply providing one-
way information. They also serve as a two-way bridge, 
receiving, synthesizing, and promptly conveying the opinions, 
concerns, and expectations of the investor community to the 
Bank's leadership, while consistently and fully responding to 
BIDV's governance messages and strategic direction in the 
market. In 2025, BIDV engaged with over 200 domestic and 
international investors, including various types of investment 
funds from countries and regions such as Vietnam, Singapore, 
Hong Kong, China, the United Kingdom, Thailand, and 
Taiwan. These meetings focused on in-depth discussions of 
the macroeconomic context, monetary policy, and BIDV's 
operational strategy, earning high praise from investors 
and partners for its professionalism and transparency. 
Analytical reports noted a positive improvement in BIDV's 
valuation and outlook; many major securities firms issued 
Buy/Positive recommendations for BIDV shares, reflecting 
market confidence in the bank's operations and development 
direction.
Simultaneously, BIDV periodically organizes earnings call 
sessions on a quarterly basis and publishes specialized 
documents for investors on the BIDV website, including the 
BIDV Investor Information Sheet and the Earnings Update 
Sheet. This not only provides timely information but also 
facilitates direct interaction between the Board of Directors, 
answers investor concerns, and gathers feedback from the 
market. 
BIDV also actively participates in domestic and international 
investment 
seminars 
and 
conferences 
to 
introduce 
and update business results and promote investment 
opportunities in BID shares, notably Vietnam Access Day 2025 
(Vietcap, Ho Chi Minh City), Emerging Vietnam 2025 (HSC, 
Ho Chi Minh City), and HOSE Daiwa Viet Nam Corporate Day 
(Daiwa, Singapore). Through these events, BIDV proactively 
conveys the Bank's strategic message to the domestic and 
international investment community, while also receiving 
assessments, recommendations, and diverse perspectives 
from financial institutions and professional investors.
In addition, BIDV conducts surveys on investor and partner 
satisfaction levels after working sessions to understand the 
needs and expectations of each target group. The survey 
results and feedback are compiled and reported to the Board 
of Directors as a basis for adjusting the content and methods 
of interaction, thereby improving the quality and effectiveness 
of investor relations.
Implement a plan to increase charter capital through a 
share offering to investors.
In 2025, BIDV actively implemented measures to increase its 
charter capital to enhance its financial capacity, meet capital 
adequacy ratios, and approach international best practices, 
specifically: (i) BIDV successfully offered nearly 124 million 
shares to 5 financial investors, thereby increasing its charter 
capital by VND1,238 billion, bringing the total charter capital to 
VND70,213 billion - placing it among the banks with the largest 
charter capital in the market. (ii) At the 2025 Annual General 
Meeting of Shareholders, shareholders approved a plan to 
further increase charter capital by 3.84% of the outstanding 
shares as of March 31, 2025, equivalent to approximately 269 
million shares, through private placement or public offering. 
Currently, BIDV is implementing the next steps to carry out the 
private placement of shares to investors in phase 2 as per the 
approved plan.
Thanks to its investor relations efforts as mentioned above, 
BIDV has been honored with numerous awards from 
prestigious organizations, including: Top 20 Most Sustainable 
Stocks in Vietnam for the second consecutive year (HOSE); 
Top 50 Best Listed Companies in Vietnam (Forbes Vietnam 
Magazine); Top 10 Best Annual Reports – Financial Sector 
for the third consecutive year (Vietnam Listed Companies 
Conference (VLCA) 2025); Outstanding Private Placement 
Transaction in 2024-2025 (Vietnam M&A Forum 2025);… 
INVESTOR RELATIONS
The Investor Relations Department – Secretariat and Shareholder Relations plays a 
bridging role between BIDV and its shareholders and the investor community through 
transparent information disclosure, ensuring the rights and interests of shareholders 
in accordance with international standards, promoting BIDV's image to attract 
potential investors, and receiving and transmitting information between the investor 
community and the Bank's leadership.
